title: Goodnight Punpun
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Punpun Onodera, drawn as a crude bird, grows from elementary school into his twenties amid a broken family, his longing for his classmate Aiko, and deepening depression. The story follows friends, a cult, and Punpun's own decline as his relationships turn destructive.
life_message: It searches for, without firmly naming, a life that is honest about pain and still open to connection.

content.note: Domestic violence, stabbings, a hammer attack and a strangulation (Wikipedia; ANN review; AniList Body Horror signal).
Sustained psychological dread and tragedy (Wikipedia; AniList Tragedy).
Sexual assault of Punpun, sexual situations involving minors and adults, fairly explicit scenes (Wikipedia; ANN; AniList Psychosexual 85%, Nudity, Rape).
A friend's father turns alcoholic and the friend takes up smoking (ANN review).
Depression, multiple suicide attempts, a hanging and a mass suicide (Wikipedia; AniList Suicide signal; MangaUpdates Abuse).
Self-harm and suicide depictions could affect vulnerable readers (to verify).

delivery.evidence: Asano said he wrote for readers who accept immorality, not to offer a role model (creator intent, Wikipedia Themes).

personified.ideology: childlike purity that rejects gray areas (Asano: 'fundamentalist')

delivery.note: The series shows failure and despair without stating a lesson, leaving readers to draw their own conclusions.

winners_losers: Almost no one wins; children of broken homes carry the heaviest losses. Sympathy goes to damaged young people, while the cult and neglectful adults are shown without sympathy.
